How the launcher is built today, and the seam for a launcher-only dark layout (read-only study; nothing edited, built or run).

ONE DOCUMENT, ONE MODEL. Every menu (launcher, its sub-pages, the in-game overlay, the title look, the Tome look, the first-start page) is the single RmlUi document res/ui/menu.rml (31 lines) styled by res/ui/menu.rcss (2330 lines), filled by one function, render() (runtime/host/frontend.cpp:3688-3969). The model is one flat vector g_rows of Row (frontend.cpp:331-350, 358) plus one index g_selected (359) and one g_screen (356). build_rows() (3990-4032) clears g_rows, calls the build_* function for g_screen, then render(). There is no notion of two focus zones anywhere. [read in code]

THE CLEANEST SEAM [inferred from the code read]:
1. A dedicated flag, not `!g_in_game`. g_in_game is only set true inside frontend_frame when a menu first opens over the game (6249); it is still false after the launcher starts a game, so the watchdog's Problem page (frontend_problem 6413, called from report.c:511/530) can run with g_in_game false. Add e.g. `bool g_launcher_up`, set true in frontend_run_launcher (4921) before run_preparing and cleared after run_menu returns (5007-5008), and a helper `launcher_dark()` = g_launcher_up && g_skin == Skin::Launcher && g_screen != Screen::Problem. "Return to launcher" over a paused game (build_in_game 3325-3339: g_screen = Launcher with g_in_game true) then keeps today's parchment look unless the owner wants it dark too (an open question for the owner).
2. One body class set in render() next to the others (3863-3892), e.g. g_doc->SetClass("launcher-dark", launcher_dark()), and when it is on, do NOT set "launcher" (3866) so none of the body.launcher parchment rules (menu.rcss:626-721) apply. All dark rules go in a new block `body.launcher-dark ...` at the end of menu.rcss, exactly as skin-title (from :1082) and skin-tome (from :1591) are done today. The class must also be added to run_preparing's clear list (4712-4714) and set there, since the first-start page writes its own markup into #menu0 under body.launcher + body.preparing (4715-4716, 4801-4810; rcss :725-785).
3. New sibling elements in menu.rml, hidden unless body.launcher-dark: a `#sidebar` (tabs), a `#hero` (title, Play button, tiles, recommended row, controller row, saves) and a dark `#help` line; #book stays as the content panel (restyled dark, position/size by rcss only). The existing #backdrop/#veil precedent (menu.rml:9,12) shows extra body-level elements that only one look uses. Nothing in the title/Tome code touches ids other than heading, menu0, menu1, note, hint, book, backdrop, backdrop-picture, veil, so new ids are inert for them.
4. render() needs a second form only in two places: (a) a new `render_launcher_dark_chrome()` that fills #sidebar and the hero panel (called from render when launcher_dark()); (b) the Launcher screen's own markup (today the generic row loop 3745-3840 emits plain centred rows). Every sub-page (Display, Sound, Graphics pages, Controls, Mapping, Mods pages, cards, roster, slots) can keep the existing row markup (.row/.label/.leader/.value/.switch/.slider/.chev/.pick/.section/.gap, .pcards/.pcard, .roster*, .tile) and be recoloured purely in rcss under body.launcher-dark, the way the Tome and title looks restyle the same markup.
5. Input: menu_step (4377-4523) assumes one vertical list. Two workable models: (i) lowest risk: the side bar IS the Launcher screen's rows (build_launcher emits one Row per tab; render draws rows of Screen::Launcher into #sidebar and a non-interactive preview/hero beside it; A or Right enters the tab = today's g_screen change; B returns, and g_launcher_row (484, 4021-4025, 4049-4050) already puts the cursor back on the tab that was opened). The existing ids row<i> and MenuListener keep working if the listener is also attached to #sidebar. (ii) MP4-style: a separate g_tab + LB/RB (kPageLeft/kPageRight, Q/E; today used only on the slot lists, 4478-4481) switch tabs while Up/Down/Left/Right stay in the panel; needs a new branch in menu_step, tab ids (e.g. tab<i>) in MenuListener, and go_back/Back rows rewritten per tab. The Play panel's three tiles side by side and the big Play button need their own navigation branch either way (precedents: move_in_roster 1895-1919 for a grid, the card_screen Left/Right jump 4461-4469).

Fonts: res/fonts ships Fira Sans Regular/Bold, IM Fell English Regular/Italic, IM Fell English SC Regular, La Belle Aurore, and Alegreya SC Regular/Bold (all SIL OFL, licence texts beside them); Alegreya SC is shipped but never loaded. Loading is Rml::LoadFontFace per file in ensure_ui (4218-4223); a new face needs one more name in that list. Existing write-up of the same structures: docs/research/in-game-menu/08-frontend-skins.md and 01-launcher-settings.md.

facts.fact: [read in code] menu_step (4377-4523): on Characters every arrow goes to move_in_roster (grid); otherwise Up/Down call move_selection(±1), which steps g_selected through g_rows with wrap, skipping rows that are disabled and have no change (4034-4041); right stick calls list_wheel when list_scrolls(). A = activate_selected (4043-4055; records g_launcher_row when on the Launcher). B (or Menu on InGame) = go_back (4057-4127: a per-screen switch; Launcher and Problem ignore Back). [read in code] g_listener is attached only to #book for Click, Mousemove and Mousescroll (4231-4236). ProcessEvent walks up from the event target to the first element whose id starts with "row", takes the index after it, and on Mousemove (only on real pointer movement) sets g_selected + render(); on Click sets g_selected, calls change(-1) if the click was on a .prev chevron else activate_selected(), then build_rows(). Wheel: roster_wheel on Characters, list_wheel when list_scrolls(). Consequences for a side bar: elements outside #book get no mouse events unless the listener is also added to them (or to body); any id beginning with 'row' is treated as a g_rows index, so tab elements must either be real g_rows entries with row<i> ids or use another prefix and their own branch.

risks: Gating the dark layout on `!g_in_game` alone is wrong: g_in_game is false after the launcher starts a game until the first in-game menu opens (frontend.cpp:6249 is the only place it becomes true), so the watchdog's Problem page (frontend_problem, report.c:511/530) would pick up the dark launcher look over a running game. Use a flag owned by frontend_run_launcher, and exclude Screen::Problem.

'Return to launcher' from the in-game menu (frontend.cpp:3325-3339) shows Screen::Launcher over a paused game with g_in_game true. With the proposed seam it keeps today's parchment launcher; the owner has not said which look that screen should have. It is a decision to ask, not to assume.

The first-start 'Preparing the game' page shares the launcher's body class and #menu0 (frontend.cpp:4712-4716, 4801-4810). If 'launcher' is no longer set, or #book moves, that page loses its layout unless it gets its own dark rules and the new class is added to its hard-coded class reset list.

RmlUi does not retry an image that failed to load once (frontend.cpp:3589-3590 comment). Disc-derived launcher art made at first start, or the owner's photo if it is optional, must only be referenced after the file exists (class gate as title-art), or it stays blank until restart.

Disc-derived art is made by run_preparing() (frontend.cpp:4660-4860) from the player's own disc before the menu shows (ensure_portraits 1590, read_disc_file 1239, write_png 1182; stamps in res/firstrun.txt), which is the existing pattern for any new disc art.

The owner asked for only the pre-game launcher, so the new layout must be gated on !g_in_game (or that in-game path will pick up the new look, or break if panels assume no game is running).

The existing input model is a single linear list (g_rows, g_selected, Up/Down, Left/Right = change) and the mouse listener resolves clicks by id="rowN" on elements inside #book (frontend.cpp:4130-4181). A side bar + tiles + buttons layout needs either every clickable thing to stay a Row with a rowN id, or new 2-D navigation and listener code; controller and keyboard must keep working, not just the mouse.

Test tooling depends on launcher behaviour: ED_LAUNCHER_TEST_KEYS presses buttons on the launcher from 1.5 s after it opens, ED_MENU_OPEN jumps to pages by name, and launcher_main_row() defines the default cursor row ('Main menu'); tools/ed/run.sh, tools/ed/jtg.sh, tools/drive.sh, tools/coop-test/play.sh and tools/run-mac.sh reference these switches or --no-launcher/ED_NO_LAUNCHER. Reordering rows or changing what A does first can silently break scripted runs.

controls::controller_name() works on the shared 'menu player'; flipping it to read both players' names and not restoring it to 0 would make later Controls pages show the wrong player. The private gamepad(player) also logs a '[controls] controller N of M' line each time it reopens a pad, so polling it every frame after a hot-plug could spam the log; use a 500 ms refresh as the Controls screen does (frontend.cpp:4511-4516).

player_has_controller(player) reports the settings choice, not whether a pad is plugged in; a controller row must combine it with connected_controllers()/controller_name() or it will claim a controller that is not there.
A GPU-name line requires changing .deps/GXRuntime (new accessor) and regenerating patches/gxruntime/eternal-darkness.patch with a VS2022 rebuild; it is the only item here that is not host-only.

Tile labels for Resolution and Frame rate are computed by locals inside build_options_rows (size_label, kScale, the choices/shown logic); copying them into the launcher risks the tile and the Options row disagreeing. Lifting them into shared helpers is safer.

Frame rate is forced to 60 in co-op by settings_apply (g_settings.mod_coop), while the stored g_settings.frame_rate is kept for solo; a tile that shows the stored value can mislead when co-op was the last mode picked. The Options row handles this with a note.
MSAA and texture filtering only change at the next start (g_running_anti_aliasing / g_running_anisotropy); if either becomes a tile it needs the same 'from the next start' wording.

The disc list is scanned once when the launcher opens and only from dump/ and the working folder; a 'no disc' panel that tells the player to drop the image in dump/ will not notice the file until the program is restarted unless a rescan is added.

Save slots have no picture or chapter; a Metroid-style saves section with thumbnails cannot be filled from existing data. Promising chapter names or screenshots needs new save-time work, and the owner's memory note says save states can go stale after code changes, so the saves section should not suggest they are permanent.
Listing memory-card saves before boot is not supported by any existing code; probing the card with dol_card_open would create an empty card file if none exists.
There is no version string in code; a footer showing 'v0.1.6' would have to be added and kept in step with the release process (.build-commit is set by hand at release).

Line numbers for controls.cpp are from the working tree, which has the owner's uncommitted test edits (all after line 1237, in the player-2 script code); do not commit that file with the launcher work.

problems.problem: Id collision in the click handler the plan describes. Tabs get ids tab<i>, and ProcessEvent is to treat 'an element whose id starts with tab' as a tab. [read in plan/rml] The container is id="tabs" (and Quit sits in #sidefoot, presumably with its own id): a click on empty space inside #tabs matches the prefix, atoi("s") is 0, and the page jumps to Play. Same family of bug the plan itself warns about for 'row' (4148-4156).
problems.fix: Name the containers so nothing but real tabs starts with the prefix (e.g. #sidebar-list, tabs as id="stab0".."stab6", Quit as id="squit"), and in ProcessEvent require a digit after the prefix and a range check before using the index. Handle Quit by its own id. Also set g_bar=false on a row Click, not only on pointer move.

problems.problem: The plan gives the 14 hashes but not what is hashed. [read on disc] Each page is 345x383 CMPR stored padded to 352x384: 67,584 bytes (image data offsets step by 0x10800; the last ends exactly at the file's 946,816 bytes). I recomputed XXH64 over those 67,584 bytes for pages 0 and 13 and got 0e3dcf592eb542ae and e155f55ec5f7b4ad, the plan's values. Copying Default's pattern (w*h/2, frontend.cpp:1621-1622) gives 66,067 bytes, every hash fails, and 'a page that fails is skipped' makes the art silently never appear.
problems.fix: Hash and bounds-check ((w+7)&~7) * ((h+7)&~7) / 2 bytes per page; decode_cmpr already skips the pad columns/rows (1287-1303). Log one line per page that fails with its computed hash. In run_preparing give the art its own need/done pair: the portraits block only runs when need_portraits (4707, 4733) and the early return (4698) must include it.

check.verdict: The plan's seams are real and mostly well read: the gate cannot be g_in_game (set at frontend.cpp:6249, never cleared), 'launcher' is a class only on the home screen (3866) so every sub-page today runs on the shared base rules, #book is rcss-placed in the launcher look (3958-3960), the test doors, controls.cpp accessors, the ignore rule and the disc facts all check out (UBookAut.tpl: 14 pages, 345x383, format 14, and the first and last hashes recomputed from the disc match), and no launcher action is dropped (Disc, Continue, Main menu, Load/Duplicate/Delete, both characters and the roster, Display, Sound, Graphics x4, Controls P1/P2 and mapping, the five Mods rows, Quit are all still reachable); kCostume is set but never read, so LB/RB are free. The order is sound in outline (gate, shell, recolour, input, panel pieces, art last) but needs four changes: set the launcher flag before the first cursor row is computed, leave the first-start page on parchment until its dark rules exist (or do step 11 right after step 2), test at 1280x960 from step 2 because that is the window's real start size and the two-card pages that root the Controls and Characters tabs do not fit beside a 30vh bar there, and split steps 3 and 4 so each can be judged from one contact sheet. The riskiest step is 4: it rewires menu_step, go_back, build_rows and the mouse listener, all shared with the in-game overlay and the title and Tome looks, and as written it lets a tab switch skip settings_save and the menu-player reset, mis-handles Left on card pages, hitches on the Display preview, has an id-prefix bug in the click handler, and can leak the bar focus into the other menus; done as 4a-4d with one on_bar() gate and one leave_page() it is safe. For disc art, nothing in the plan puts a disc picture in git or in the Windows zip, but the Deck and Mac package scripts copy the working res folder as it is, so the new autopsy folder (like today's portraits) would ride along there unless those scripts are guarded.
